{{Short description|Cryptography standard}}
{{Correct title|title=PKCS #8|reason=hash}}
In [[cryptography]], '''PKCS #8''' is a standard syntax for storing [[private key]] information.  PKCS #8 is one of the family of standards called [[PKCS|Public-Key Cryptography Standards (PKCS)]] created by [[RSA Laboratories]]. The latest version, 1.2, is available as RFC 5208.<ref>{{cite IETF
| title = Public-Key Cryptography Standards (PKCS) #8: Private-Key Information Syntax Specification Version 1.2
| rfc = 5208
| last1 = Kaliski
| first1 = B.
| date = May 2008
| publisher = [[Internet Engineering Task Force|IETF]]
}}</ref>

The PKCS #8 private key may be encrypted with a [[passphrase]] using one of the PKCS #5 standards defined in RFC 2898,<ref>{{cite IETF
| title = PKCS #5: Password-Based Cryptography Specification Version 2.0
| rfc = 2898
| last1 = Kaliski
| first1 = B.
| date = September 2000
| publisher = [[Internet Engineering Task Force|IETF]]
}}</ref> which supports multiple encryption schemes.

A new version 2 was proposed by S. Turner in 2010 as <nowiki>RFC 5958</nowiki> <ref>{{IETF RFC|5958}} - Asymmetric Key Packages</ref> and might obsolete <nowiki>RFC 5208</nowiki> someday in the future.

PKCS #8 private keys are typically exchanged in the [[Privacy-enhanced Electronic Mail|PEM]] [[base64]]-encoded format, for example:<syntaxhighlight lang="pem">
